tagline: Isan's dinosaur town — Praewa silk, Lam Pao Dam, and the Phu Phan range
introHtml: Kalasin is a quiet Isan town with more to see than you'd expect. This is one of Thailand's richest dinosaur fossil sites — the Sirindhorn Museum and the Phu Kum Khao excavation pit let you walk up and look at real bones. The south of the province runs into the Phu Phan range, with waterfalls and viewpoints, while the Kham Muang and Kuchinarai districts are Phu Thai country, home to the hand-woven Praewa silk the province is known for. Around the town, Lam Pao Dam draws people for fish by the water. If you like easygoing Isan trips with real nature, history, and craft, Kalasin is worth a stop.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable — ideal for heading up Phu Phan and visiting the dinosaur dig

highlights.name: Phu Kum Khao dinosaurs
highlights.blurb: Kalasin is Isan's dinosaur town. In Sahatsakhan district you'll find the fossil excavation pit and the Sirindhorn Museum, which keeps real skeletons on display.

highlights.name: Praewa silk
highlights.blurb: The Praewa-pattern silk of the Phu Thai people around Kham Muang district is the province's signature — fine, hand-woven, and a craft still very much alive.

highlights.name: Lam Pao Dam
highlights.blurb: A large earthen dam near town where Kalasin locals come to catch the breeze and eat fish by the water, with Dok Ket beach for a swim in the hot season.

highlights.name: Phu Phan range
highlights.blurb: The mountains across the south of the province, full of waterfalls, forest, and viewpoints — a stretch of nature that runs through several districts.

highlights.name: Phu Thai culture
highlights.blurb: Kham Muang and Kuchinarai districts are Phu Thai country, still keeping their language, dress, and traditional weaving.

highlights.name: Phra Phrom Phumipalo
highlights.blurb: A large Buddha image standing in the middle of a reservoir at Sahatsakhan, clearly visible from the shore — a natural pairing with a Phu Kum Khao visit.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, all eaten with sticky rice — found all over town, with the bold, real-deal Isan punch.

foodScene.name: Lam Pao Dam freshwater fish
foodScene.note: Restaurants along Lam Pao Dam serve fresh fish — grilled, tom yum, and fish larb — eaten by the water in the cool breeze.

foodScene.name: Isan sausage and mam
foodScene.note: Sour fermented meats grilled and eaten with fresh vegetables and sticky rice — a snack and a local souvenir.

foodScene.name: Pla ra and jaew bong
foodScene.note: Pla ra (fermented fish) and jaew bong chili dip are kitchen staples in Kalasin, easy to find at fresh markets — hot and eaten with raw vegetables.

foodScene.name: Mu krata and jim jum
foodScene.note: Mu krata grill spots and jim jum hot pots are all over town — a favorite dinner for workers and families.

foodScene.name: Phu Thai food
foodScene.note: Around Kham Muang and Kuchinarai you'll find Phu Thai home cooking like chicken soup with vegetables, plus local ferments with their own distinct taste.

foodScene.name: Cafes and coffee
foodScene.note: The town has a number of new cafes — an easy place to sit with a coffee mid-day before heading back out.

foodScene.name: Morning markets and street food
foodScene.note: Markets in town have grilled pork with sticky rice, khanom chin, and grilled snacks to graze on from morning till evening.

attractions.name: Sirindhorn Museum
attractions.blurb: The dinosaur museum in Sahatsakhan district, displaying skeletons and the story of the prehistoric era — a key fossil learning center in Thailand.

attractions.name: Phu Kum Khao excavation pit
attractions.blurb: The real dinosaur fossil dig next to the Sirindhorn Museum, where you can see bones still set in the rock layer right where they were found.

attractions.name: Lam Pao Dam
attractions.blurb: A large earthen dam where Kalasin locals come to relax, with Dok Ket beach for a hot-season swim and fish restaurants by the water.

attractions.name: Kaeng Ka-am Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A waterfall on the Phu Phan range in Na Khu district, with a wide rock platform and clear water — good for a swim and a break in the rainy season.

attractions.name: Phu Sing and Pha Sawoei
attractions.blurb: A viewpoint on Phu Phan in Somdet district, looking out over the ridges and a sea of mist in winter — a worthwhile stop on the way up Phu Phan.

attractions.name: Khok Kong Phu Thai cultural village
attractions.blurb: A Phu Thai village in Kuchinarai district that still keeps its traditional ways, with performances and weaving to see on home ground.

attractions.name: Ban Phon Praewa silk center
attractions.blurb: Ban Phon in Kham Muang district is a Praewa silk-weaving hub — watch the hand-weaving steps and buy cloth straight from the villagers.

attractions.name: Phra Phrom Phumipalo in the water
attractions.blurb: A large Buddha image standing in the middle of a reservoir at Sahatsakhan, clearly visible from the shore — revered, and a signature photo spot for the town.
